questions.q: A gardener measures a bamboo cane as 2 3/10 7/100 m. Three pupils copy the length on to plant labels: Label A says 2 37/100 m, Label B says 237/100 m and Label C says 23 7/100 m. (a) Which labels show the cane's true length? Give a reason. (b) By how many hundredths of a metre does the wrong label overstate the length? (c) A 13/100 m tip is tied on to the cane. Write the new length in units and tenths.
questions.a: (a) Labels A and B. 3 tenths = 30 hundredths, so 2 3/10 7/100 = 2 37/100, and 2 units = 200 hundredths, so it is also 237/100. (b) Label C is 23 7/100 = 2307/100, and 2307 - 237 = 2070 hundredths too much (that is 20 7/10 m). (c) 237/100 + 13/100 = 250/100 = 2 50/100 = 2 5/10 m.
s: (a) Picks Labels A and B, using 1 tenth = 10 hundredths and 1 unit = 100 hundredths
(b) Writes Label C as 2307/100 and gets 2070 hundredths too much
(c) Gets 250/100 and writes it as 2 5/10 m

questions.q: A science club's model grasshopper is 6 2/10 3/100 cm long. Its abdomen is 3 7/10 8/100 cm and its thorax is 1 6/10 9/100 cm; the rest is its head. (a) Add the abdomen and the thorax, regrouping where needed. (b) Find the length of the head, showing what you split at each place. (c) Check your answer to (b) by writing all three lengths in hundredths only.
questions.a: (a) 4 units, 13 tenths and 17 hundredths: 17 hundredths = 1 tenth 7 hundredths, and 14 tenths = 1 unit 4 tenths, so the total is 5 4/10 7/100 cm. (b) 6 2/10 3/100 - 5 4/10 7/100: split 1 tenth into 10 hundredths to get 6 1/10 13/100, then split 1 unit into 10 tenths to get 5 11/10 13/100. Subtracting gives 0 units, 7 tenths and 6 hundredths, so the head is 7/10 6/100 cm. (c) 623 - 378 - 169 = 76 hundredths = 7/10 6/100 cm, the same.
s: (a) Regroups hundredths and tenths and gets 5 4/10 7/100 cm
(b) Splits a tenth and a unit and gets the head as 7/10 6/100 cm
(c) Uses 623 - 378 - 169 = 76 hundredths and confirms the answer

questions.q: A saffron trader in Pampore compares two pairs of weights, in kg. Sameer, his helper, says: '40 thousandths is more than 3 hundredths, and 3 tenths is more than 400 thousandths.' (a) Write all four weights as decimals. (b) Which part of Sameer's statement is right and which is wrong? (c) How many thousandths equal 3 tenths? Use this to give one way of comparing such weights safely.
questions.a: (a) 40 thousandths = 0.04, 3 hundredths = 0.03, 3 tenths = 0.3, 400 thousandths = 0.4. (b) The first part is right: 0.04 > 0.03. The second is wrong: 0.3 < 0.4, so 3 tenths is less than 400 thousandths. (c) 3 tenths = 300 thousandths. Write both weights in the same unit first (300 thousandths and 400 thousandths); only then does the larger count mean the larger weight.
s: (b) Says the first part is right and the second wrong, since 0.3 < 0.4
(c) Gets 300 thousandths and says to change both to the same unit before comparing

questions.q: A treasure-hunt clue at a maths club describes a number. It has 2 tens. Its units digit is 3 times its tens digit. Its tenths digit is 0. Its hundredths digit is 3 more than its units digit. Its thousandths digit is double its tens digit. (a) Write the number in decimal notation and read it aloud correctly. (b) Write it in the form used for place value, such as 7 × 1 + 5 × 1/100. (c) The tenths and hundredths digits are swapped by mistake. By how much does the number increase?
questions.a: (a) 26.094, read as twenty-six point zero nine four (not 'twenty-six point ninety-four'). (b) 2 × 10 + 6 × 1 + 9 × 1/100 + 4 × 1/1000 (with 0 × 1/10 in the tenths place). (c) The swap gives 26.904, and 26.904 - 26.094 = 0.81, so it increases by 0.81.
s: (a) Writes 26.094 and reads it digit by digit after the point
(c) Forms 26.904 and finds the increase 0.81

questions.q: A kirana shop's billing machine prints weights in kg with three digits after the point, such as 5.030, 12.600, 0.750 and 20.400. To shorten its bills, the shop sets it to delete every 0 that comes after the point. (a) Write what it now prints for each of the four weights. (b) Which printed weight has changed in value, and by how many grams? (c) State the rule the machine should follow instead.
questions.a: (a) 5.3, 12.6, 0.75 and 20.4. (b) Only 5.030 has changed: 5.030 kg is 5.03 kg but 5.3 kg is printed, and 5.3 - 5.03 = 0.27 kg = 270 g too much. The other three lost only zeros at the right end. (c) Delete only the zeros at the right end, after the last non-zero digit. A zero between the point and a later digit holds a place and must stay, so 5.030 should print as 5.03.
s: (b) Names 5.030 as the only one changed, by 270 g
(c) States that only zeros at the right end may go; a zero before a later digit must stay

questions.q: Four parcels at a post office are weighed on different machines. The slips read: Parcel P, 34 tenths of a kg; Parcel Q, 340 hundredths of a kg; Parcel R, 3400 thousandths of a kg; Parcel S, 304 hundredths of a kg. Reena says R is the heaviest because 3400 is the biggest count. (a) Write each weight as a decimal. (b) Is Reena right? Explain using place value. (c) How many grams lighter than P is the lightest parcel?
questions.a: (a) P = 3.4 kg, Q = 3.40 kg, R = 3.400 kg, S = 3.04 kg. (b) No. P, Q and R are the same weight: each is 3 units and 4 tenths, and the zeros at the right end add nothing. Thousandths are smaller pieces, so more of them are needed for the same weight. (c) S is the lightest: 3.4 - 3.04 = 0.36 kg = 360 g.
s: (b) Says No: P, Q and R all equal 3 units 4 tenths, so a bigger count of smaller parts is not a bigger weight
(c) Picks S and gets 360 g

questions.q: A generator's fuel dipstick has equally spaced marks numbered 0, 1, 2, and so on. Only two are labelled: mark 3 shows 4.6 L and mark 7 shows 5.4 L. (a) How many litres does one gap between marks stand for? (b) What does mark 0 show? (c) The fuel stands at 5.7 L. Does it reach a numbered mark? If not, say which two marks it lies between and where.
questions.a: (a) From mark 3 to mark 7 there are 4 gaps covering 5.4 - 4.6 = 0.8 L, that is 8 tenths shared by 4 gaps, so each gap is 2 tenths = 0.2 L. (b) Mark 0 is 3 gaps below mark 3: 4.6 - 0.6 = 4.0 L. (c) The marks show 4.0, 4.2, 4.4 and so on, so mark 8 is 5.6 L and mark 9 is 5.8 L. 5.7 L is on no mark; it lies exactly halfway between marks 8 and 9.
s: (a) Uses 4 gaps for 0.8 L to get 0.2 L a gap
(b) Gets mark 0 = 4.0 L
(c) Says it is on no mark and lies halfway between mark 8 (5.6 L) and mark 9 (5.8 L)

questions.q: In a yogasana contest Pooja scores 7.41 and Lata scores 7.3986. Lata's coach says: 'Lata's digits 9, 8 and 6 are big, and Pooja has only a 1 after her 4, so Lata may be ahead.' (a) Find the first place where the two scores differ, and say who is ahead. (b) Is the coach right to worry about the later digits? Compare Lata's score with 7.4 to explain. (c) What is the smallest digit d for which a score of 7.d1 is greater than 7.49?
questions.a: (a) Both have 7 units, but Pooja has 4 tenths and Lata has 3 tenths, so the first difference is in the tenths and Pooja is ahead. (b) No. After 3 tenths, Lata's digits add less than 1 more tenth: 7.3986 is still 0.0014 below 7.4, and even 7.3999 would be below 7.4. Pooja's 7.41 is above 7.4. So once a place decides, later digits cannot change the result. (c) d = 5: 7.41 is less than 7.49 because 1 hundredth is less than 9 hundredths, while 7.51 is greater because 5 tenths is more than 4 tenths.
s: (a) Finds the first difference in the tenths place and says Pooja is ahead
(b) Says No: 7.3986 is below 7.4 (later digits add less than one tenth) while 7.41 is above it
(c) Gets d = 5, rejecting 7.41 and accepting 7.51

questions.q: A health centre in Almora stores tablets of 250 mg each, packed in strips of 10 tablets. (1 g = 1000 mg, 1 kg = 1000 g.) (a) Write the weight of one tablet in grams as a decimal. (b) Write the weight of one strip in grams and in kilograms. (c) The storekeeper says 400 strips of tablets weigh 1 kg. Check her claim, working in milligrams first.
s: (a) Writes 0.25 g
(b) Writes 2.5 g and 0.0025 kg
(c) Says she is right: 1,000,000 mg = 1000 g = 1 kg

questions.q: A trust in Nashik pays three scholarships of ₹1,250.50, ₹2,075.25 and ₹960.40. Its computer stores every amount in paise, but one month a fault makes it read the stored number as rupees. (a) Write what the computer stores for each scholarship. (b) Find the total the trust meant to pay, in rupees. (c) Find the total that was actually sent. (d) How much extra was sent in all, in rupees? (e) Another student was sent ₹75,025 because of the same fault. What should she have received, and in what way is the place value of each digit changed by the fault?
questions.a: (a) 125050 paise, 207525 paise and 96040 paise (1 rupee = 100 paise). (b) ₹1,250.50 + ₹2,075.25 + ₹960.40 = ₹4,286.15. (c) 125050 + 207525 + 96040 = 428615, so ₹4,28,615 was sent. (d) ₹4,28,615 - ₹4,286.15 = ₹4,24,328.85 extra. (e) The stored number 75025 means 75025 paise = ₹750.25. Each digit is read two places too far to the left, so every digit is worth 100 times its true value.
s: (a) Writes 125050, 207525 and 96040 paise
(b) Gets the intended total ₹4,286.15
(c) Gets ₹4,28,615 sent
(d) Subtracts with the point aligned and gets ₹4,24,328.85 extra
(e) Gets ₹750.25 and says each digit is worth 100 times its true value

questions.q: Medicines cost ₹276.35 and the customer pays with a ₹500 note. The cashier in Hubballi does not subtract. She counts up: 'Add something to reach ₹277, then something to reach ₹300, then something to reach ₹500.' (a) Find the change by column subtraction, showing where you borrow. (b) Write the three amounts she counts up and add them. (c) Explain why both methods must give the same answer.
questions.a: (a) Write 500 as 500.00. Borrowing through the zeros: 10 - 5 = 5 hundredths, 9 - 3 = 6 tenths, 9 - 6 = 3 units, 9 - 7 = 2 tens, 4 - 2 = 2 hundreds, giving ₹223.65. (b) ₹0.65 to reach ₹277, ₹23 to reach ₹300 and ₹200 to reach ₹500: 0.65 + 23 + 200 = ₹223.65. (c) The difference 500 - 276.35 is the amount that must be added to 276.35 to make 500. The cashier builds that same amount in three easy steps, and 276.35 + 223.65 = 500 confirms it.
s: (a) Writes 500.00, borrows across the point and gets ₹223.65
(b) Gives ₹0.65, ₹23 and ₹200 with total ₹223.65
(c) Explains that the difference is what must be added to 276.35 to reach 500

questions.q: Rain has blotted four digits on a slip from a honey cooperative in Wayanad. It shows, in kg, 36.P58 + Q7.43R = 64.1S7, where P, Q, R and S are single digits. Work column by column from the right, as in column addition. (a) Find R, and say whether anything is carried. (b) Find S. (c) Find P, and say what is carried to the units column. (d) Check the units column and find Q. (e) Write the full sum and check it by a subtraction.
questions.a: (a) Thousandths: 8 + R must end in 7, so R = 9; 8 + 9 = 17, so 1 is carried to the hundredths. (b) Hundredths: 5 + 3 + 1 = 9, so S = 9, with nothing carried. (c) Tenths: P + 4 must end in 1, so P = 7; 7 + 4 = 11, so 1 is carried across the point to the units. (d) Units: 6 + 7 + 1 = 14, which gives the 4 shown, and 1 is carried. Tens: 3 + Q + 1 = 6, so Q = 2. (e) 36.758 + 27.439 = 64.197. Check: 64.197 - 27.439 = 36.758.
s: (a) Finds R = 9 with 1 carried to the hundredths
(b) Finds S = 9 using the carried 1
(c) Finds P = 7 with 1 carried across the point
(d) Confirms 6 + 7 + 1 = 14 and finds Q = 2
(e) Writes 36.758 + 27.439 = 64.197 and checks by subtraction

questions.q: Two courier boxes together weigh 42.3 kg. The first weighs 17.6 kg, and the label on the second is torn. A clerk uses Sonu's rule (the sum is greater than the sum of the whole-number parts and less than 2 more than that) and says: 'The second box's whole-number part can only be 24 or 25.' (a) Test the whole-number parts 23, 24, 25 and 26 in the rule. (b) Is the clerk right? (c) Find the exact weight of the second box and say which of the clerk's two values it matches.
questions.a: (a) With whole part 23 the sum lies between 40 and 42, which leaves out 42.3. With 24 it lies between 41 and 43, and with 25 between 42 and 44, and both include 42.3. With 26 it lies between 43 and 45, which leaves out 42.3. (b) Yes: only 24 and 25 fit the rule. (c) 42.3 - 17.6 = 24.7 kg, so the whole-number part is 24.
s: (a) Gives the four ranges 40-42, 41-43, 42-44 and 43-45
(b) Says the clerk is right, since only 24 and 25 include 42.3
(c) Gets 24.7 kg, matching 24

questions.q: A painter in Sivakasi mixes 13.47 L of white paint with 28.86 L of blue. A helper records the total as 42.52 L. (a) Use the whole-number parts to give the two whole numbers between which the sum must lie. Does this catch the helper's total? (b) Now use the units and tenths of each number instead: 13.4 and 28.8. Show that 42.52 cannot be right, without doing the full addition. (c) Find the exact total.
questions.a: (a) 13 + 28 = 41, so the sum lies between 41 and 43. 42.52 is in this range, so the check does not catch it. (b) 13.4 + 28.8 = 42.2, and what is left of each number is less than 0.1, so together less than 0.2. The sum lies between 42.2 and 42.4. Since 42.52 is more than 42.4, it cannot be right. (c) 13.47 + 28.86 = 42.33 L.
s: (a) Gives 41 and 43 and says 42.52 is not caught
(b) Gets the range 42.2 to 42.4 and rejects 42.52 as above it
(c) Gets 42.33 L

questions.q: A school health card writes ages as years.months, so 11.5 means 11 years 5 months. Aarti's card says 12.3, her brother Neel's says 9.11 and their cousin Tara's says 9.9. (a) Say why the point here is not a decimal point. (b) Tara says: 'I am older than Neel because 9.9 is greater than 9.11.' Decide whether she is right. (c) Find the true age gap between Aarti and Neel, and show that subtracting the cards as decimals gives a wrong result.
questions.a: (a) A year has 12 months, not 10, so the number after the point counts months, not tenths. (b) She is wrong. 9.11 is 9 years 11 months and 9.9 is 9 years 9 months, so Neel is 2 months older, although 9.9 > 9.11 is true for decimals. (c) 12 years 3 months - 9 years 11 months: borrow a year as 12 months to get 11 years 15 months, and the gap is 2 years 4 months. As decimals, 12.3 - 9.11 = 3.19, which would wrongly suggest 3 years and more.
s: (a) Says a year has 12 months, so the digits after the point are not tenths
(b) Says Tara is wrong: Neel is 2 months older
(c) Gets 2 years 4 months and shows the decimal result 3.19 does not match

questions.q: At a school swimming meet the board shows times as minutes.seconds, always with two digits after the point. So 1.05 means 1 minute 5 seconds. The four relay swimmers show 1.52, 2.07, 1.48 and 1.59. (a) Write 1.52 and 2.07 in minutes and seconds. (b) A parent subtracts as decimals and says the second swimmer was 0.55 slower than the first. Find the true gap in seconds. (c) Find the team's true total time in minutes and seconds, and compare it with what adding the readings as decimals gives. (d) Write 1 minute 48 seconds as a true decimal number of minutes, using 6 seconds = 1/10 minute. (e) The coach says: 'These readings can be put in order like decimals, but they cannot be added like decimals.' Is the coach right? Justify using these readings.
questions.a: (a) 1 minute 52 seconds and 2 minutes 7 seconds. (b) From 1:52 to 2:00 is 8 seconds, and 7 more makes 15 seconds, not 55. (c) Minutes: 1 + 2 + 1 + 1 = 5. Seconds: 52 + 7 + 48 + 59 = 166 seconds = 2 minutes 46 seconds. The true total is 7 minutes 46 seconds, but adding as decimals gives 6.66. (d) 48 seconds is 8 lots of 6 seconds, so 8 tenths of a minute: 1.8 minutes, which is not the same as the board's 1.48. (e) Yes. With two digits always shown, comparing from the left compares minutes and then seconds, so 1.48 < 1.52 < 1.59 < 2.07 is the true order. Adding fails because 60 seconds, not 100, make the next unit: the decimal total 6.66 is wrong.
s: (a) Writes 1 min 52 s and 2 min 7 s
(b) Finds the true gap of 15 seconds
(c) Gets 7 min 46 s and contrasts it with the decimal sum 6.66
(d) Writes 1.8 minutes
(e) Agrees with the coach: order works (1.48 < 1.52 < 1.59 < 2.07) but adding fails because 60 seconds make a minute

questions.q: At a village mela, visitors guess the weight of a pumpkin that really weighs 6.4 kg. The guesses are Anu 6.39, Bala 6.5, Chinu 6.41, Dev 6.375 and Esha 6.04. (a) Find how many thousandths of a kg each guess is from 6.4. (b) Who is closest? Is there one winner? (c) One more visitor wants to beat the best guess so far with a guess of exactly three digits after the point, other than 6.400. What are the lowest and the highest such guesses that would win?
questions.a: (a) Anu 10, Bala 100, Chinu 10, Dev 25, Esha 360 thousandths. (b) Anu and Chinu are both closest, 10 thousandths away, one below and one above, so they tie and there is no single winner. (c) The guess must be less than 0.010 kg from 6.4, so the lowest is 6.391 and the highest is 6.409 (each 9 thousandths away).
s: (a) Gives the five gaps 10, 100, 10, 25 and 360 thousandths
(b) Says Anu and Chinu tie, with no single winner
(c) Gives 6.391 as the lowest and 6.409 as the highest
